name: Invoke-ACLScanner - Find Dangerous AD ACL Entries
description: Invoke-ACLScanner from PowerView finds dangerous ACL entries in Active Directory: GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDACL, WriteOwner, and other exploitable permissions over users, groups, computers, and GPOs. Reveals attack paths that BloodHound maps visually but this tool finds via direct LDAP queries.
notes:
=== BASIC USAGE ===
  Import-Module PowerView.ps1
  Invoke-ACLScanner -ResolveGUIDs
  # Export results:
  Invoke-ACLScanner -ResolveGUIDs | Export-Csv acl_scan.csv -NoTypeInformation

=== FILTER BY RIGHTS ===
  # Only GenericAll:
  Invoke-ACLScanner -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match "GenericAll"}
  # Only WriteDACL:
  Invoke-ACLScanner -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match "WriteDacl"}
  # Only WriteOwner:
  Invoke-ACLScanner -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match "WriteOwner"}

=== CHECK SPECIFIC OBJECT ===
  Get-ObjectAcl -SamAccountName <target_user> -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match "GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner"}

=== EXPLOITABLE PERMISSIONS ===
  GenericAll:    Full control - reset password, add to group, modify
  GenericWrite:  Modify attributes - Kerberoast, Shadow Creds, logon script
  WriteDACL:     Modify permissions - grant yourself GenericAll
  WriteOwner:    Take ownership - then grant yourself full control
  ForceChangePassword: Reset password without knowing current
  AddMember:     Add yourself to a group

=== FROM LINUX (alternative) ===
  # dacledit (impacket):
  dacledit.py <domain>/<user>:<pass> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -target <target_dn> -action read
  # BloodHound with SharpHound:
  SharpHound.exe -c ACL

recommended.note: BloodHound provides visual ACL attack path mapping.

defense.why_it_works: AD object ACLs are readable by any authenticated user. Invoke-ACLScanner enumerates all ACEs and highlights those that grant dangerous rights to non-privileged principals.
defense.impact: Identifies all ACL-based attack paths: password resets, group membership changes, delegation abuse.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1069.002] Bulk LDAP ACL queries; PowerView script execution; large LDAP result sets.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell script block logs with Invoke-ACLScanner; LDAP queries for nTSecurityDescriptor.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows sourcetype=WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-ACLScanner*"
| table _time, ComputerName, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("Invoke-ACLScanner", "Get-ObjectAcl")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AdditionalFields
defense.prevention: Audit and minimize dangerous ACL entries; use AdminSDHolder for protected groups; monitor ACL enumeration; implement least-privilege ACLs.

detections.name: ACL enumeration via PowerView
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName == "powershell.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-ACLScanner", "Get-ObjectAcl", "Get-DomainObjectAcl")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Security audit teams running authorized AD assessments
detections.tuning: Also detect by LDAP query patterns reading nTSecurityDescriptor on many objects
